messages:
alex_s: FYI customer 'lumina-pay' on Private VPC hitting 502s and TLS timeouts to our inference endpoint in eu-west-1. Started ~08:02 UTC.
maria_net: Can you paste the curl + tcpdump you ran? need to know if it's DNS, TLS handshake, or firewall drop.
alex_s: quick repro I ran from their NAT instance:
```
$ curl -v --resolve api.lumina.redwood:443:10.0.5.12 'https://api.lumina.redwood/v1/predict' --connect-timeout 5
*   Trying 10.0.5.12:443...
* connect to 10.0.5.12 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to api.lumina.redwood port 443: Connection timed out
```
alex_s: tcpdump captured SYNs but no SYN-ACKs, then occasional RSTs from 10.0.0.1 (their FW). snippet:
```
12:08:03.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > 54.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
12:08:03.223789 IP 10.0.0.1.40000 > 10.0.5.12.54321: Flags [R], seq 0
```
maria_net: RST from 10.0.0.1 suggests an inline firewall/NAT device rejecting flows. Ask customer to check SG outbound, NACL egress rules, and any inline FW policies that shadow SGs.
dan_oncall: @maria_net note: we recently rolled a control-plane egress allowlist update for model telemetry that tightened ephemeral port ranges for private clusters. Could that be blocking their ephemeral source ports?
maria_net: Possibly. Common misconfig: NACLs ordered to DENY before ALLOW or SG referencing 0.0.0.0/0 but NACL more restrictive. Ask them to run `aws ec2 describe-network-acls` and paste the egress entries.
alex_s: Customer returned this NACL egress block:
```
Rule 100: DENY ALL 0.0.0.0/0
Rule 200: ALLOW TCP 443 54.12.34.56/32
```
alex_s: They have a blanket DENY (higher priority) that blocks all ports before the specific allow for our endpoint — that's why tcp shows no SYN-ACK.
maria_net: Yep. NACLs are evaluated by rule number order; DENY 100 will short-circuit. Two remediation options: 1) Move the ALLOW to a lower rule number than the DENY, or 2) remove the broad deny and rely on SG stateful filtering.
jordan_prod: Also check stateful SG on the instance: if outbound allowed but return path blocked by NACL, connection will fail. Suggest workaround: add specific ALLOW for source ephemeral port range (1024-65535) to that remote destination/port (443), or open ephemeral range entirely for that subnet.
alex_s: Customer tried adding an SG egress rule for 443 -> our endpoint but kept failing until they moved the NACL rule. After moving their ALLOW to rule 50 it started working.
alex_s: Quick notes for support doc: - NACLs are stateless and order matters. - SGs are stateful: allow outbound but NACL deny will still kill handshake. - Inline third-party FW may RST flows even if SG/NACL look permissive.
dan_oncall: adding: if TLS handshake starts then fails with unknown_ca, verify SNI and ALPN; but in this case tcp handshake never completes so it's network layer.
maria_net: Can we add a check we run when customers report 443 timeouts? small triage checklist:
- verify DNS resolves to expected private IP
- tcpdump for SYN / SYN-ACK / RST
- aws ec2 describe-security-groups and describe-network-acls
- check route tables for NAT gateway / inline FW
- if RSTs reference gateway IP, ask vendor firewall team for policy logs
alex_s: I'll update the support ticket with repro steps and recommend moving the ALLOW ahead of the DENY or opening ephemeral port range. Customer marked as P2, will follow up.
deploy-bot: Deployment "nacl-rollout/prod" succeeded at 1716123475 (note: unrelated infra change)
maria_net: thanks — closing loop once customer confirms change in prod. :thumbsup:
